transcript.text: hotpoint SA2 oven not heatin on fan, grill ok. wat does SA2 mean??

SA2 is the Hotpoint oven series/range prefix, rather than an error code or an explanation of the fault. An exact model normally has extra letters/numbers after it on the rating label. Because the grill works but fan cooking does not heat, the fan-oven element is the leading possibility, followed by the function selector/temperature control. First rule out the simple control-state issue: with the oven cool, select the fan symbol with a ring around it (not the fan-only/defrost symbol), set about 180°C, and make sure the clock is showing manual mode rather than AUTO or a flashing timer. Does the temperature indicator come on, and after 10–15 minutes is there any warmth at all?
clock is in manual yes. conventional top+bottom does heat but slowly. on fan setting barely warms, fan at back isnt spinning just a low hum

The low hum with the rear cooking fan not turning points first to a seized or failing fan-oven motor; a blade catching the rear cover is the other possibility. Do not keep running it while it hums, as that can overheat the motor. With the oven completely cool, switched off and isolated, see whether the blade turns freely and smoothly through the rear guard openings—do not remove the rear panel or force it. If it is stiff, stuck or scraping, the motor/blade assembly needs an engineer; if it turns freely but only hums when selected, the motor or its start circuit is still likely. The weak fan heat may also mean the fan-oven element needs testing, so an engineer should assess both rather than assuming only one fault.
isolated it at the cooker switch first. blade is very stiff n feels gritty when i turn it by hand. had a slight hot smell from the back once but not now

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The fan-oven motor is very likely seized: a gritty, stiff blade together with a hum is the usual bearing/motor failure pattern. The engineer should also test the fan-oven element, as the lack of fan circulation explains the weak fan cooking but does not fully rule out an element fault. The slow conventional heating may be a separate element/control issue, so mention that at the same visit.
